final_candidates.decision_summary: C52 is the critical lower axial thiolate ligand coordinating the heme iron in human CBS. Mutating C52 to Ala abolishes heme binding and severely destroys catalytic activity.
H65 acts as the upper axial histidine ligand to the heme iron. Substitution to Ala disrupts heme coordination, preventing proper active-site architecture and abolishing enzyme function.
Replacing the axial thiolate donor C52 with Ser disrupts the mandatory iron-thiolate bond, causing profound loss of catalytic turnover.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 mutations targeting key catalytic/heme-binding residues have been prioritized and verified against the wild-type sequence.

history.rationale: K119 forms the essential covalent Schiff base internal aldimine with the PLP cofactor; mutating it to alanine eliminates PLP binding and abolishes CBS catalytic activity.
K119 is the essential catalytic Schiff-base lysine that binds PLP; substitution to Ala completely abolishes PLP cofactor binding and enzyme activity.
C52 is a primary axial ligand coordinating the heme iron in human CBS; C52A disrupts heme binding and severely impairs enzyme function.
C52 acts as a required axial thiolate ligand for heme coordination in CBS; C52A abolishes heme binding and drastically reduces catalytic function.
H65 acts as the second axial ligand for the heme cofactor; replacing it with alanine disrupts heme coordination and abolishes catalytic function.
H65 serves as the second axial ligand coordinating heme iron; mutation to Ala destroys heme binding and abolishes enzyme activity.
Arginine substitution at K119 preserves positive charge but lacks the primary amine needed to form the Schiff base with PLP, resulting in loss of function.
K119R removes the primary amine necessary for PLP Schiff-base formation, severely impairing/abolishing catalytic turnover.
Substituting C52 with serine alters the thiolate coordination to the heme iron, causing heme loss and inactivation of CBS.
C52S replaces the axial cysteine thiolate, disrupting normal heme coordination and causing significant loss of catalytic activity.
Steric hindrance and charge alteration from H65R disrupt the axial heme ligation site, causing enzyme loss of function.
H65R disrupts axial heme iron coordination, preventing proper heme pocket formation and activity.
